messages.author: baefdba1eb5ae15d
messages.subject: memory leak with pystan?
parts:
Hi all,

I'm trying out pystan on some very simple model and have run into a memory blowup issue, with pystan quickly consuming 10+GB of ram. 

Here's the code:

def run_gaussian(magnitude=1, T=1000, K=10, model=None):
params, x, y = data_gen.generate_data(T, magnitude, K)
data = { 'T' : T,
'K' : K,
'x' : x,
'y' : y,
'sigma0' : 1,
'mu0' : 0,
'sigma' : 1,
}
iter = 1000
chains = 2
if model is None:
fit = pystan.stan(file='gaussian.stan', data=data, iter=iter, chains=chains)
else:
fit = model.sampling(data=data, iter=iter, chains=chains)
return fit, params, x, y


And here's the model ('gaussian.stan'):

data {
int<lower=0> T;  // number of data points
int<lower=0> K;  // data dimension
matrix[T, K] x;
vector[T] y;

real<lower=0> sigma0;  // prior variance of mean
real mu0;             // mean of coefficients
real<lower=0> sigma;   // observation variance
}
parameters {
vector[K] theta;       // coefficients
}
model {
for (k in 1:K) 
theta[k] ~ normal(mu0, sigma0);
for (t in 1:T)
y[t] ~ normal(x[t] * theta, sigma);
}

Using pystan.stan does not cause a problem (with the default settings it runs almost instantaneously and uses minimal memory).
The problem occurs if I run:

In [1]: g_model = pystan.StanModel(file='gaussian.stan', model_name='gaussian_model')
In [2]: fit, params, x, y = run_gaussian(model=g_model)

My os is Mavericks. 

Thanks,
Jonathan

parts:
Hi Jonathan,

There was an issue like this awhile back:

https://github.com/stan-dev/pystan/issues/10

Does the problem occur if you call model.sampling twice? What if instead
of returning the fit you return fit.extract()?

Thanks,

Allen

messages.author: baefdba1eb5ae15d
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] memory leak with pystan?
parts:
Allen: Thanks for pointing me to that bug report. The problem does appear to be related to naming of models. A memory explosion occurs if (a) I create a named model and call sampling or (b) I create two models (they don't need to be named) and call sampling on either one. There is no memory explosion with one, unnamed model.

This is enough information for me to work around the problem for now (I think). Should I open a new bug report? 

Jonathan
